title: Implement adaptive queue-drain + graceful-scale to prevent hosted GPU exhaustion
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: After the 2026-02-25 hosted API incident we saw prolonged GPU queue buildup that led to aggressive throttling and customer-facing 503s. Root cause combined a recent scheduling heuristic regression (lowered preemption headroom) and a bursty traffic pattern from a single high-throughput tenant. This ticket tracks delivering an adaptive queue-drain mechanism, improved autoscaler hysteresis, and a controlled graceful-scale flow to avoid repeated exhaustion events.
impact_summary: Multiple customer requests experienced tail latency >10s and soft-503s during sustained bursts. Estimated token loss / dropped requests ~0.3% of peak traffic during the incident window; revenue/SLAs impacted for enterprise customers on hosted tier.
incident_timeline: 2026-02-25 09:12 UTC - Spike begins from tenant T-Alpha (large batch generation job)
2026-02-25 09:18 UTC - Node pool p99 latency crosses 2s, admission starts shedding requests
2026-02-25 09:22 UTC - Autoscaler failed to rapidly add GPU nodes due to aggressive cooldown/hysteresis
2026-02-25 09:27 UTC - Runtime scheduler regression (PR #12031) reduced preemption headroom, making eviction slow
2026-02-25 09:40 UTC - Throttling rules amplified queue build-up, partial 503s observed
2026-02-25 10:05 UTC - Manual intervention: force-scale + emergency fair-shed applied; recovered by 10:22 UTC
root_cause_analysis: Regression in scheduler PR #12031 removed optimistic preemptive draining in certain bin-packing paths
Autoscaler configured with 10m scale-down grace and 3m cool-down, which was too slow for multi-minute bursts
Admission control did not consider in-flight KV cache size; large KV cache occupancy per request increased effective GPU memory pressure
Single tenant produced thousands of concurrent long-sequence generation requests without client-side rate limiting
decision_log: Ship adaptive queue-drain that can preempt low-priority requests and prioritize short-sequence requests to reduce tail latency
Lower aggressive autoscaler cooldowns during sustained high queue length and add a fast-path opportunistic prewarm
Introduce per-tenant soft-rate limits and token-bucket enforcement as a backstop to single-tenant storms
Keep scheduler regression revert as contingency; prefer targeted heuristic patch to retain throughput gains
action_items: A1: Implement adaptive queue-drain in runtime - prototype + unit tests (owner: Miguel Santos) - due 2026-03-18
A2: Autoscaler tuning: introduce 'queue-aware' scaling policy and reduce cooldown when queue_length > Q_HIGH (owner: Lena Zhang) - due 2026-03-22
A3: Admission control: add KV-cache-aware admission scoring and short-request fast-track (owner: Connor Blake) - due 2026-03-20
A4: Tenant safeguards: soft-rate limit pilot for top-50 tenants + customer comms (owner: Maya Rivera, PM) - due 2026-03-26
A5: Dashboard & alerts: add queue-depth SLOs, per-pool preemption headroom metric, and runbook link (owner: Observability team) - due 2026-03-16
A6: Rollback plan: keep revert PR ready (PR #12500) if adaptive drain causes regressions - owner: Miguel Santos - due 2026-03-18
implementation_notes: Adaptive queue-drain algorithm: maintain two queues (short/long). When pool queue depth exceeds Q_HIGH, proactively preempt from long queue up to X% of in-flight low-priority requests and promote short queue requests.
Preemption will prefer requests with low KV-cache footprint to avoid costly reloads; KV cache estimator added to request metadata to enable scoring.
Autoscaler fast-path: if sustained queue_length > Q_CRITICAL for T_SHORT, trigger opportunistic prewarm nodes (non-blocking) with reduced cooldown and higher max-burst limit.

Add a circuit-breaker that transitions pool to 'graceful-degrade' mode when p99 latency > L_HIGH and queue_growth_rate positive for 3 minutes. In degrade mode, apply stricter fair-shed and reject known large-batch patterns first.
Will run canary release on 5% of pools for 48h with telemetry comparing: tail latency, throughput, token-cost, and eviction rate. Canary groups chosen across regions (us-east1, eu-west1).
testing_plan: Unit tests for drain scheduler and KV cache estimator
Integration tests: simulate tenant spike with synthetic load generator (loadgen-v2) to validate queue drain behavior and autoscaler triggers
Chaos test: induce node-loss during drain to ensure graceful-fallback and maintain SLOs
Performance benchmark: measure p50/p95/p99 latency delta and cost-per-token impact pre/post feature with 10k request burst
rollout_plan: Step 1 (Canary): Deploy to 5% of hosted GPU pools, monitor 48h - metric targets: p99 latency <= baseline+10%, queue drop rate reduced by >=50%
Step 2 (Region expansion): If canary stable, expand to 30% pools with 24h validation windows
Step 3 (Full): Gradual roll to 100% over 72h with autoscaler safeguards and rollback watch
Communication: Notify support and customer success prior to canary; publish postmortem summary and mitigation steps for enterprise customers
monitoring_and_alerting: New metrics: pool.queue_length, pool.queue_growth_rate, pool.preemption_evictions, pool.kv_cache_occupancy_per_req
Alerts: QueueGrowthCritical (queue_growth_rate > 50rps sustained 2m), PreemptionSpike (>500 evictions/min), AutoscaleCooldownMiss (scale_needed but cooldown active > expected)
Dashboards: 'GPU Pool Health' with short/long queue breakdown, per-tenant top-n contributors, and canary vs baseline comparison
review_feedback: PM (Maya Rivera): prefer soft-rate limits over hard kills for customers with enterprise agreements; ensure comms plan
Design (Lena Zhang): KV cache estimator should be conservative to avoid misclassifying long requests as low-footprint
SRE (Anika Bose): add runbook steps for manual forced-scale and safe draining; include commands and TTLs
Security (Ravi Kumar): no additional secrets required; confirm telemetry does not leak request payloads
followups_and_longer_term: F1: Explore model-aware scheduling: prioritize small-context models during bursts (audit models by average context size) - cycle 2026-Q2
F2: Per-tenant SLA throttles and governance UI in Console so customers can opt-in to 'bulk-job' safe lanes
F3: Evaluate smarter KV cache eviction policies to reduce per-request cache footprint during contention
notes: Status update 2026-03-04: Prototype queue-drain implemented; initial microbench shows 40% reduction in p99 for mixed workloads
Status update 2026-03-10: Autoscaler queue-aware policy merged to staging for integration tests
Status update 2026-03-14: Canary scheduled; observability dashboards ready; targeted comms drafted
